As a member of the Sales Engineering team (a subset of Project Delivery), this role exercises independent technical judgment to develop cost-optimized, execution-ready multi-MW plant solutions aligned with Mainspring's linear generator capabilities. The Staff Sales Engineer is accountable for architectural integrity, commercial rigor, and seamless transition from concept through execution, including a clean handoff of the design basis, estimate, and scope assumptions to Project Management and Project Engineering at contract award. For large-load and data center sites, define at the proposal stage how the plant serves and protects the load, including islanding, load-following, black start, and transfer schemes. Define plant controls, communications, and protection scope (PPC, SCADA/EMS, utility telemetry, protective relaying, revenue metering) and the grid code (IEEE 1547/2800), ISO/RTO, and NERC requirements that drive equipment selection and cost. Delivery Discipline & Commercial Rigor Produce complete, accurate, and timely proposal packages, including responses to utility, IPP, and data center developer RFPs, across multiple concurrent projects. Develop EPC scopes of work and responsibility matrices that clearly split scope between Mainspring, the customer, EPC partners, and the utility, and that carry cleanly into contracts and project execution. Identify technical and commercial risk in customer specifications and contract terms (performance guarantees, availability, grid code compliance, interconnection cost exposure) and drive resolution before award. Evaluate site constraints that affect plant feasibility and cost, including gas fuel supply (pressure, flow, delivery infrastructure), power density and layout, hazardous area requirements, and air permitting. Cross-Functional Collaboration Collaborate with Engineering, Product, Controls, Commissioning, Interconnection, Supply Chain, and Project Management to support technical feasibility and execution alignment. Feed lessons learned from grid-scale pursuits back into reference designs, estimating tools, and proposal templates. Working knowledge of medium-voltage (5 kV+) plant electrical systems, including collector systems, step-up transformers, gen-ties, switchgear, and the plant-side interface to the utility substation or point of interconnection. Familiarity with utility interconnection processes (Feasibility, System Impact, and Facility Studies) and applicable standards and grid codes (NEC, NESC, IEEE 1547/2800, ISO/RTO requirements, NERC reliability standards). Experience estimating balance of plant and EPC scope for multi-MW facilities, including MV equipment, civil/structural, and fuel systems. Strong understanding of standard electrical drawings such as wiring diagrams, electrical schematics, one-lines, P&IDs, and civil site plans. Ownership Mentality: Proactive in identifying risks and comfortable advocating for the resources needed to solve them. review_candidates.description: About The Team The Storage organization builds and operates the online stateful systems and abstractions that DoorDash Engineering depends on: reliable, efficient, secure, and easy to use. Within Storage, the Distributed Key Value team owns the storage platform that powers business-critical workloads across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. These systems sit on the Tier-0 critical path. They serve millions of QPS across multiple regions and underpin how hundreds of engineering teams build reliable systems at massive scale. About The Role DoorDash's storage abstraction platform is a unified data-access layer that sits in front of our databases and decouples application teams from the underlying storage engines, similar to modern data-gateway and key-value / time-series data-abstraction platforms. Nearly every request that touches persistent data flows through it. As DoorDash scales 10x–100x across new verticals, global expansion, and acquisitions, this platform is where the hardest distributed-storage problems live — latency at the tail, request routing, and reliability under exponential load. We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer to be the domain specialist for the storage abstraction platform: a deep, opinionated technical leader who owns the reliability, performance, and correctness of the platform at scale, sets its technical direction, and raises the execution bar across the storage organization. You must be located in the New York Metro Area, Bay Area or Seattle for this hybrid position. You will report to the Engineering Manager on our Distributed Key Value team within the Storage organization. You're excited about this opportunity because you will… Own the reliability, performance, and correctness of the storage abstraction platform at scale, independently leading resolution of mission-critical issues in ambiguous, high-pressure situations. Set technical direction for the platform — the storage abstraction and data-access layer, provider model, caching, and routing — owning the architecture, quality, and long-term approach as it scales. Work deep in the data plane — proxy, KV, CDC, and routing — on the problems that define a Tier 0 system: p99/p999 latency, request routing, hot partitions, GC/MVCC behavior, and failure isolation. Shape the client surface — thin/thick providers, polyglot code generation, and SDKs — that connects application services to the platform. Act as a force multiplier and trusted technical advisor: raise the execution and quality bar for your team and partners, mentor senior engineers, and influence roadmaps beyond your immediate scope. Take end-to-end ownership of the platform lifecycle — guiding customers from onboarding through adoption, driving the offering forward and expanding its impact. Design and operate systems built for 100x growth, proactively engineering for exponential load rather than reacting to it, and eliminating single points of failure through documentation, automation, and shared ownership. Translate ambiguous business needs into durable, storage-owned solutions, and be an opinionated domain expert on how storage problems are best solved. We're excited about you because… 10+ years building large-scale distributed systems, with deep expertise in at least one Tier 0 storage / data-plane system (distributed KV, database internals, caching, or a storage proxy/control plane). Experience with storage abstraction layers or data-access gateways that decouple applications from the underlying databases — e.g., data-gateway or key-value / time-series data-abstraction platforms, or comparable in-house systems. Deep experience building or operating a large-scale distributed data store — such as DynamoDB, RocksDB, or ZippyDB — is an equally strong fit. Expertise in low-latency, high-throughput systems — tail-latency optimization, hot-partition and load balancing/routing, backpressure, and failure isolation. Devin executes long-horizon tasks across sandboxed environments, spawns subagents, uses tools, and does all of this at scale across millions of sessions. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home. Our impact Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that. Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts About The Team Even a simple configuration error can lead to significant unintended usage. At HighLevel, we aim to build robust systems that protect our customers and the platform from accidental surges and intentional abuse alike. This team creates the intelligent safeguards that ensure our automation remains safe and reliable for everyone. We are looking for a Staff Engineer to architect the future of Trust, Controls & Safety. You will lead the technical direction of a real-time platform that secures critical workflows across HighLevel—including Signups, SaaS checkouts, User management, and global communication usage. This system processes 160M+ events and $4M+ in transactions daily, serving as the essential foundation for platform integrity. The challenge is to build a highly available, low-latency control plane that balances strict enforcement with a seamless user experience. By integrating synchronous metering with asynchronous signal correlation, you will help us stay ahead of evolving fraud vectors while ensuring that legitimate business activities, from new user signups to complex SaaS billing cycles, proceed without friction. As a Staff Engineer, you'll set the technical direction, own the hardest problems on the platform, mentor engineers across squads, and partner closely with EMs, PMs, Finance, Risk, Support and the channel teams. Getting this right means customers stop getting bills they didn't intend, and abuse stops being a cost the honest majority carries. Codify patterns that make good engineering repeatable Hands-on leadership: Write code, design systems, and debug production issues. Distributed Systems Mastery: Deep expertise in concurrency, event-driven architectures, and consistency primitives (CAS, atomic dry-runs, idempotency). Financial Rigor: Experience with systems where code correctness has direct financial impact—metering, ledgers, or payment gateways. Operational Instinct: A track record of technical leadership through influence, driving architecture for multi-team platforms from design to production.
